This document outlines the major 
maintenance
procedures P2,
which must be performed every five years as indicated by Y5
in the title block.

items:
A work permit must be issued and 
 personnel carrying out the maintenance should be trained and qualified or 
 directly supervised by some one who is.

CB must be isolated and proper earthling at the two sides of the CB is
 required.
Safety fence with caution marks around the work area is required.
Isolate control circuit (DC voltage).
Wearing safety helmet is required
Use only fiberglass ladders.
Close the through valve (1 fig 2).

Open the drainage valve (24 fig 1) to drain the air out of the tank and be
 sure that the breaker is free of pressure. The pressure can be read at the
 control pressure gauge placed in the control cubicle.

Mobile crane - Triple sheaved - Sufficient and suitable polypropylene rope
 to lower arcing chambers and hollow support insulators to ground.

One set of metric open end box wrenches , one set of socket wrenches,
 Allen keys (No 5 & 6) - Adjustable spanner - open end spanners (No 41
 & 45) - One set of screwdrivers -Torque wrench.
Fine file - Fine emery paper - Wipers.
Hammer kg - Hammer 2 kg - Rubber hammer.

Tin cans to hold bolts, nuts, studs, washersetc, 
 complete set of gaskets and 3 injectors .

Previous overhaul report including 
 all tests, Bituminous pain.

Release

 17

Raise

Take

Pull

sections.text:
Inspection of the moving contact (13 fig
4 )

items:
If its surface is in a good condition it means that the fixed contact
 is probably also in good condition and there is no need to disassemble it.

If its surface is slightly burnt it should be cleaned by a fine file and a
 fine emery paper, then placed again in its previous position into the arcing
 chamber.

If
 it is burned and punctured to a depth of 1-2 mm it should be changed and
 overhaul maintenance should be made to all other parts of the arcing chamber
 to change the screen(19 fig 4), gliding segment contacts (20 fig 4), moving
 contact (13 fig 4) and fixed contact (6 fig 3).

Release 4 bolts (22 fig 4 ) and bring them out of the cylinder ( 12 fig 4
 ).Use screwdriver
Unscrew the screen to release it and pull it out.
Change it with another complete one.

At the end screw in the 4 bolts and tighten them
 properly. Use screwdriver

items:
Release the
 control relays of moving contact ( 5 fig 4 ) by releasing the nuts

Release the
 control outlet relay ( 4 fig 4 )Use spanner 13

Release entire
 base of the valves (30-31-32 fig 2) by releasing the 4 nuts (23 fig 4 )
 gradually by half turn all around.

Pull out the entire base, moving contact spring (9 fig 4) ,moving contact
 tube (13 fig 4 ) and the cylinder (12 fig 4 ).

Release the cylinder (12 fig 4 ) and pull out the segment contact (20 fig
 4) along with the two springs which control the position of segment contacts
 .

Inspect all the parts and change the moving contact tube ( 13 fig 4), the
 sliding segment contacts, the two rings of the cylinder (12 fig 4) and the
 internal gasket of the head of the cylinder.

Assemble the whole set of the moving contacts once again to be ready to
 place it in its previous position after finishing the maintenance of the
 fixed contact and replace it in the arcing chamber.

Insert the special spanner 6003014 into the arcing chamber to release the
 counter nut (33fig3).
With the special spanner 6003015 unscrew the fixed contact.
Unscrew the position screws ( 46 fig 5). Use screw driver
Release the head (45 - 44 fig 5 ) by means of special spanner 361021.

Change the head (44 - 45 fig 5 ) completely and connect it with contact
 tube (43 fig 5).

Tighten the
 position screw ( 46 fig 5 ) properly.

Replace the
 fixed contact in its place into the arcing chamber

Before replacing the parts of arcing chamber clean all parts
 and the internal insulator surface of the arcing chamber with dry cloth,
 then grease the moving contact slightly with the contacts grease.

Prior to definite tightening of the counter nut (33 fig
 3), the measure (D fig 3) must be 391 mm.

Replace the moving contact in its place into the arcing
 chamber

sections.text:
Disassemble
the entire base of the valves (30-31-32 fig 2) to make maintenance as following:

items:
Release the six
 bolts (74 fig 4 ) by means of allen key No 6 to disconnect the outlet valve
 ( 31 fig 2) out off the base of the two control relays (30 fig 2 ).

Change the
 gasket (26 fig 4) .

Check the plate
 with gasket ( 25 fig 4) and change it complete if needs to be changed
Release the four nuts of the metal cover of the valve. Use spanner 17
Release the nut (54 fig 4) to release the piston and the lower gate.
Change the piston ring and the gasket of the gate. Use spanner 19
Assemble the outlet valve once again .

sections.text:
Disassemble the outlet relay (32 fig. 2 also re. to
fig. 7 for more detail in performing mtce)

items:
Release the two nuts of the studs which holding it over the outlet
 valve. Use spanner 13
Raise it up.

Release the four nuts which hold the parts and lift the cover (77 fig
 7).Use spanner 10

Change the gaskets (38 and 76 fig 7) and the gasket of the opening D
 take care that all gaskets are properly placed onto their seats .

sections.text:
Disassemble the control relay (30 fig. 2 also re. to
fig. 6 for more detail )

items:
Release the four nuts which assemble its parts and lift the cover. Use
 spanner 10
Change all gaskets and take care that all are properly onto their seats.

sections.text:
Maintenance of pneumatic relay: (1 fig. 9 also re. to
fig. 10 for more detail )

items: Separate the relay from its support
Unscrew the guide (27 fig. 10) with special spanner (361024
Unscrew the nut (28 fig. 10)
Remove the cover (29 fig. 10)

Change the gasket (25 fig. 10) and it must be glued to the body by means
 of universal gum
Change the piston ring (28 fig. 10) and valve (26 fig. 10)
Clean all the parts of the relay and all the openings.

Reassemble the relay and no lubrication is required but care should be
 taken that the gaskets are properly laid in their slots.

sections.text: Maintenance of the air tank and return pressure valve

items:
Remove the two covers of the inspection holes which one of them is
 provided with return pressure valve (26 fig 1)Use spanner 24

Clean the tank from dirtiness and possible condensate by a flow of
 compressed air and vacuum machine.

If the internal surfaces are rusty it should be cleaned by metal brush
 then twice coated with bituminous coating.
Change the two gaskets of the inspection holes covers
Repaint the outside surface of the air tank.

Clean
 the return pressure valve, check the gasket (30 fig. 15)and spring (32
 fig. 15) change them if it need

sections.text:
Regulating
of the safety valve (28 fig1) see fig 17.

items: Take off the cap (121 fig 17). Use spanner 19
Release the counter nut (120 fig 17). Use spanner 10

By rotating the nut (119 fig17) regulate the desired pressure which can
 be seen at the pressure gauge in the control cubicle.

Clean the filter (27 fig17) and dried its filtering
 element (33 fig 18) at a temperature less than 80 
 C until all humidity has evaporated. Use spanners 24, 41, 45 & Allen 5

After finishing the maintenance of all the CB parts
 reassemble it once again as in its previous position and recheck the
 tightening of all nuts and bolts by torque wrench.

Recharge the CB with air and visually check all the
 feeding pipes.

Before putting in service perform micro ohm and timing
 tests, record the results, compare with previous test
 results and report / investigate significant changes.
Finally record all results on maintenance card.
